summary: Two things closed this week and the client closed both of them herself. The Aug 1-14 invoice finally landed - 'Hi everything is sent!' on 8/26 - but only after her direct question of 8/18 about the $1,000/day Zelle cap on the new account sat unanswered for eight days; Stephski's only intervention was a chase on 8/26 ('Checking back in on this') that answered nothing. Terms expired 8/22, so the invoice went four days late, exactly as last week's report predicted, and by exactly the same mechanism that made the June 15-30 invoice late: new bank details plus the $1k cap plus no receipt confirmation. Two days on, nobody has acknowledged that the money arrived. The second closure is worse to read: on 8/28 Shayna set up Notion herself - 'Hii I just set up notion' - and handed Fred her email for the invite. That is the tracker she asked for on 7/20 and explicitly said she did not want to sign up for a tool to get. It took 39 days and she did the work. Fred sent exactly one message in the entire seven-day window, on 8/23, and it was another ask: when is she back, because 'we had a big push on Jim  for one'. That is the second consecutive week in which Fred's only output to this client is a request for content. Her reply on 8/24 - 'Hi I get home the 26th. Please let chatters know this' - has sat unacknowledged for four days. Meanwhile every structural item aged another week: the fans who paid for VIP on a full-nude promise are 17 days without a refund, a substitute, an audit or a chargeback check and have still never been mentioned again; her Aug 7 untracked-custom question is 21 days unanswered; the vault-notes rule is 22 days; the PG mass-message folder 23 days; the time-waster filter 31 days; and she still does not know who replaced the chatter Fred removed on 8/11. Real positives: money in the bank, a third consecutive clean week on feed posts (that complaint can close), Michelle's leak report on time on 8/25 for the eighth straight week, Mayson proactively booking the monthly call, and Shayna home from Africa on 8/26 and immediately re-engaged.

The single acute risk carried into this week did resolve: the Aug 1-14 invoice was paid in full by 8/26. That is why the drop is only two points rather than ten. But it resolved late (7-day terms expired 8/22; completed 8/26) and it resolved without ALTR doing anything - her 8/18 question about whether the new Zelle recipient reset her $1,000/day cap was never answered by anyone, and Stephski's single message in the window was a chase on 8/26, eleven days after issue, that gave her no total, no confirmation and no alternative. Two of the last four invoice cycles have now run late and both immediately followed a banking change. Nobody has yet confirmed receipt, two days after she said everything was sent - the exact confirmation she halted payment mid-installment for on 7/5. Against that: not one of the six overdue commitments moved. The fans who paid for VIP after being promised full nude are now 17 days with no refund, no substitute, no audit and no chargeback check, and the word has not been spoken in the chat since 8/11. Her Aug 7 custom question is 21 days old. The replacement chatter Fred promised on 8/11 has never been named, so she still does not know who is working her account. Fred contributed one message in seven days and it was a request for a custom; when she answered it on 8/24 with a direct instruction ('Please let chatters know this') he did not reply, and four days later still has not. The tracker did unblock, but because the client signed up for the tool she had refused to sign up for - a 39-day agency task discharged by the customer. Offsetting positives that stopped this being a bigger drop: full payment received, third clean week on unauthorized feed posts (23 days since the 8/5 auto-scheduler disconnect - this complaint can now close), Michelle's eighth consecutive on-time leak report on 8/25 thanked the same week, Mayson proactively booking the monthly check-in, and a client who came home on 8/26 and is still opening messages with 'Hi hi' rather than an escalation.
